chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabī, who said:
A man asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the Bedouins: Is jihad incumbent upon them? He said: “There is no jihad upon them unless Islam is feared for, in which case their help is sought.”
He said: Then do they have any share from the jizyah? He said: “No.”

key_terms.جِهَادٌ: armed striving or military struggle in defense of Islam
key_terms.فَيُسْتَعَانَ بِهِمْ: their assistance is sought or they are called upon for help
key_terms.ٱلْأَعْرَابِ: the Bedouins or desert-dwelling Arabs being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْإِسْلَامِ: the religion whose safety and security are being considered
key_terms.ٱلْجِزْيَةِ: the poll tax mentioned here in relation to legal entitlement

ai.seo_question: Are the Bedouins obligated to perform jihad, and do they receive any share from the jizyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the Bedouins, stating that jihad is not ordinarily obligatory upon them unless there is fear for Islam and their assistance is needed. It also rules that they have no share in the jizyah, indicating a distinction in legal entitlement and obligation.
